record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does the undirected s-t connectivity problem admit a simple, direct proof that it belongs to catalytic logspace CL, where CL means CSPACE(O(log n), n^{O(1)}), i.e. deterministic computation with O(log n) ordinary workspace plus polynomially many catalytic bits that must be restored exactly on halting?

evidence.quote: Definition 3. The class CL is defined as CSPACE(O(log n), nO(1)).
Problem 2. Give a simple, direct proof of uSTConn ∈ CL.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the catalytic logspace class CL = CSPACE(O(log n), n^{O(1)}) as follows. A catalytic Turing machine has three tapes: a read-only input tape of length n, a read/write work tape of length O(log n), and a read/write catalytic tape of length n^{O(1)}. The catalytic tape is initialized with an arbitrary string w (the catalytic content). The machine is deterministic and, for every input x and every initial catalytic content w, must halt with the catalytic tape restored to exactly w. A language L is in CL if there exists such a machine that, for every w, correctly decides membership of x in L while satisfying the restoration condition.

Let uSTConn denote the undirected s-t connectivity problem: given an undirected graph G on n vertices and two specified vertices s and t, decide whether there exists a path from s to t in G.

Problem: Provide a simple, direct proof that uSTConn ∈ CL. Here "direct" means a proof that does not proceed by appealing to the inclusion L ⊆ CL together with the known result that uSTConn ∈ L (i.e., not by invoking Reingold's logspace algorithm or any equivalent derandomization of random walks on expanders via the zig-zag product), but instead exhibits an explicit catalytic-logspace algorithm for uSTConn whose correctness and restoration property can be verified directly.
artifact.status_search_result: No published direct catalytic-logspace algorithm for undirected s-t connectivity (other than appealing to Reingold's theorem uSTConn ∈ L and L ⊆ CL) appears in the literature. The problem is posed as an open question in the catalytic-computation research program and no resolution was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Undirected connectivity in log-space (Reingold)
status_evidence.snippet: Deterministic log-space algorithm for undirected s-t connectivity, giving uSTConn ∈ L (hence trivially in CL).
status_evidence.claim: uSTConn is in L, so it is in CL via the trivial inclusion L ⊆ CL, but this is not a direct catalytic-space construction.

status_evidence.title: Catalytic logspace and bipartite matching (search summary)
status_evidence.snippet: Catalytic space results have been developed for problems like bipartite matching; no direct CL algorithm for uSTConn was located.
status_evidence.claim: The question of a direct CL algorithm for uSTConn does not appear to be resolved in the located literature.
